claim:
Short version: the window is a classic Qt tabbed application — eight bordered tabs across the top, a status bar doing the talking, text-only buttons, group boxes, a combo/checkbox/button row beside the search field. That idiom reads as 2012 regardless of colour. The palette and type scale in `theme.py` are actually fine; the age comes from structure and chrome, not from the colours. (Caveat: there are no screenshots in the repo, so this is from reading the layout code, not from seeing it rendered.)

What "ultra modern" looks like for this app in 2026, concretely:

**The search box becomes the app.** On an empty index or empty query the window is one large centred field with a few suggested searches under it — Raycast/Spotlight, not Explorer. Results grow beneath it. This is the eight-year-old benchmark taken literally.

**Tabs become a left rail.** A narrow icon rail (Search, Files, Mail, Code, Offline Media, Reports, Settings) with Indexing demoted to a small progress pill at the bottom of the rail. The top tab strip goes.

**Controls become chips.** Scope becomes a segmented control under the box; `/type pdf` filters appear as removable pills once typed; the four checkboxes (drag out, pinned, timeline, grid) become icon toggles in one toolbar row. Interpret and rerank move into the View/⋯ menu.

**Results become borderless rows.** 8–12px radii, no gridlines, a 20–24px type icon, hover tint rather than a border, highlight runs drawn as a tinted background instead of bold. `ResultDelegate` already exists, so this is a repaint rather than a rebuild.

**Preview becomes an inspector.** A right pane that slides in with a metadata header (kind, size, date, path) above the content, rather than title/subtitle labels over a stacked widget.

**Chrome and materials.** Frameless window with a custom title bar (the search field can live in it, as VS Code and Arc do), rounded corners, Mica backdrop on Windows 11 via the DWM attribute, one SVG icon set (Fluent or Lucide) recoloured per theme — there are currently no icons at all. Settings group boxes become Windows 11-style expander cards.

**Feedback.** Status-bar messages become inline toasts on the existing `NoticeBar`; long waits show skeleton rows; pane toggles fade rather than snap.

Two things worth knowing before wanting it. All of this is reachable in Qt Widgets with QSS, delegates and a frameless window — Qt Quick would give better motion but is a rewrite, which "working version first" rules out. And the ready-made route, PyQt-Fluent-Widgets, is GPL for the PyQt6 build with a paid commercial licence **(UNCONFIRMED — check before adopting, since you intend to publish)**. claim:
That settles it: go branded and OS-agnostic, not native-Fluent. Mica, acrylic and Fluent icons have no counterpart on macOS, and mimicking each OS natively means two chromes to maintain and neither quite right. Linear, Raycast, Arc and Obsidian all look at home on both platforms precisely because they own everything below the title bar and borrow nothing from either OS. That is the model.

The suggestion, built on that:

**Keep the native title bar on both.** Frameless windows are the single biggest cross-platform pain — on macOS you lose traffic lights, fullscreen and window dragging unless you re-implement them. Own the window contents, not the frame. This also means Mica is off the table, which is fine.

**Left rail, not tabs.** Sidebars are the native idiom on macOS (Finder, Mail, Notes) and the current Win11 idiom too, so one layout satisfies both. Rail entries: Search, Files, Mail, Code, Offline Media, Reports, Settings; Indexing as a progress pill at the rail's foot.

**Brand palette from the splash, applied with restraint.** Navy `#15084B` as the accent and rail tint in dark mode, the three stripe colours reserved for kind badges (green code, blue document, orange mail) so they carry meaning rather than decoration. Light mode keeps the current near-white surfaces with navy accent. The existing `theme.py` token set already supports this; it is a palette change, not new plumbing.

**Lucide icons.** ISC licence, monochrome SVG, recolourable per theme, looks neutral on both platforms. Fluent reads as Windows; SF Symbols cannot be shipped outside Apple platforms.

**System font per OS, which you already do.** The scale in `theme.py` is expressed relative to the system font, so Segoe UI Variable on Windows and SF Pro on macOS come free. The only fix is `splash.py`, which hardcodes Segoe UI.

**Overlay scrollbars.** macOS hides scrollbars until you scroll; Windows shows them. A thin custom overlay (the QSS scrollbar already has no steppers) makes both feel the same.

**Add a menu bar now.** macOS requires one and Leasha has none; Qt puts a `QMenuBar` in the mac system bar automatically. On Windows it can be hidden behind a ⋯ button. Doing it now avoids retrofitting 3,600 lines of `shell.py` shortcuts later. Your `Ctrl+K`-style bindings already map to ⌘ on macOS in Qt, so those survive.

**Borderless rows, chips, inspector preview, inline toasts** — as before; none of that is OS-specific.

Two items from your own parked census fit here: `hotkey.py` and `selection.py` are already marked "redesign" for macOS, and the PySide6 draft matters more once publishing on two platforms is real, because of PyQt6's GPL.
